title: Spring timing gave no clear mean summer flow forecast gain at Ob and Yenisey in 1980-2017
abstract: We applied a published Lena spring timing forecast method at Ob-Salekhard and Yenisey-Igarka. Separate expanding fits used earlier certified ArcticGRO v20261104 records from 1936. The June 30 baseline used April-June mean flow and mean summer flow in five earlier retained seasons. The candidate added the half-volume date of April-June flow. The target was August-September mean flow. In 38 common test years, 1980-2017, timing reduced mean squared error by 14.35% at Ob and raised it by 11.51% at Yenisey. The mean basin gain was 1.42%, with conditional 95% three-year block limits of -17.82% to +16.13%. All planned mean-score checks included zero. The test gives no clear shared gain and does not exclude physical timing effects. This is a separate basin extension using the same data product, not an independent measurement system. Revised data, retrospective certification, regulation, two basins and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and an arithmetic audit support reproduction. External records and derived record-level tables remain outside the signed package.
